title: kate-lsp: poll the server for events
summary: poll drains every body the reader thread has queued without blocking and returns them as ServerEvent values: published diagnostics, a response to one of our requests with its method, a request from the server, a log or show message, or a notification the client ignores. The window calls poll on a timer.

lane.reason: A Cursor cloud agent codes this packet. The crate is pure Rust, the test runs a fake server over pipes on Linux, and the backlog marks the LSP client CLOUD.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: poll first moves the held bodies from wait_for, then try_recv until Empty or Disconnected. textDocument/publishDiagnostics deserializes to Diagnostics; window/logMessage and window/showMessage give Log with the message text; a Response whose id is in pending gives Response with the method and removes it; a Request is passed through; other notifications are dropped. Extend tests/client.rs with hover_response_arrives_through_poll: after initialize, request textDocument/hover with a position, loop poll with a 10 ms sleep up to 5 seconds, and assert a Response for hover whose result is Ok and not Null. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: client::hover_response_arrives_through_poll
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because poll does not exist. After the change the hover response arrives as a Response event named hover.
